# Stratified single-cell limits: atomic centers, low-rank centers, and canonical lifts

This note supplies two unconditional centerpoint statements for actual
single-cell limits and one structural conditional transfer. It retains
hollow projections and nonaffine perpendicular support graphs. The general
positive-rank sharp functional theorem is not proved here.

The input is exactly the joint measure Brunn--Minkowski inequality proved
in `candidate 185fb6155f830e0e`:
finite nonzero compactly supported measures mu_z, indexed by a finite
P subset Z^n, satisfy, at every positive-weight convex combination with
integer output z=sum_i theta_i z_i,

    mu_z(sum_i theta_i E_i)^(1/N)
      >=sum_i theta_i mu_zi(E_i)^(1/N),                    (1)

for compact positive-mass E_i. The output is present and nonzero.
The continuous ambient space is arbitrary; N>=1 is an integer.
Throughout this note depth_mu(y) means UNNORMALIZED halfspace mass:
inf{mu(H): H is a closed ambient halfspace containing y}. Divide every
displayed depth bound by the total mass W to obtain normalized depth.
The intended rate setting additionally has q_z<N, where q_z is the affine
dimension of the support S_z. All measures, masses, and halfspaces below
are in the actual original physical coordinates unless explicitly lifted.

## 1. Weighted colored atomic centerpoint in arbitrary affine embeddings

Let G be a nonempty finite set in any finite-dimensional real affine
space, with k occupied labels. Assume that whenever distinct g,h have the
same label, their actual geometric midpoint (g+h)/2 belongs to G. The
midpoint need not initially have that label. Give the points arbitrary
positive weights w_g of total W. Then there is g_* in G such that

    sum_(g in H intersect G) w_g >= W/k                   (2)

for every closed ambient halfspace H containing g_*. This is the scoped
colored-midpoint theorem already proved in
`candidate 58dcf29bfb78a573`,
Section 7. The following self-contained proof records precisely what is
needed for the rate application; no integer coordinates in the embedding
and no affine graph hypothesis are required.

First, any finite system a_i(x)<=b_i missing G has a subsystem of at most
k inequalities missing G. Choose eta>0 smaller than
min_(g in G) max_i(a_i(g)-b_i), and let beta_i=b_i+eta.
Choose T_i>max{beta_i,max_G a_i}. Among threshold vectors t in the compact
box beta_i<=t_i<=T_i whose STRICT systems a_i(x)<t_i miss G, maximize
sum_i t_i. This feasible set is closed: for each g at least one of the
finitely many inequalities a_i(g)>=t_i must hold.

Each nonsaturated index i has a witness g_i with a_i(g_i)=t_i and
 a_j(g_i)<t_j for every j!=i. Otherwise a small threshold increase
preserves exclusion, by finiteness of G, contradicting maximality.
The witnesses are distinct. Two with the same label have a midpoint in G
strictly satisfying every inequality, a contradiction. Thus there are at
most k nonsaturated indices. Saturated inequalities exclude no point of
G, and the corresponding nonsaturated ORIGINAL inequalities are stronger
than the strict relaxed ones. They give the desired subsystem.

This implies the same relative Helly bound k for finite families of
polytopes, by their halfspace descriptions. For arbitrary convex sets E,
replace E by conv(E intersect G). It is contained in E and has exactly
the same trace on G. The relative Helly bound follows without any
closedness premise on E.

Now take the finite family conv(A), over all A subset G with
w(A)>W-W/k. Any at most k such sets have a common point of G by the
union bound on their complements. Relative Helly gives g_* common to all
of them. If a closed halfspace H through g_* had weight less than W/k,
its complementary trace A=G minus H would have weight greater than
W-W/k. Its entire convex hull lies strictly outside H, contradicting
g_* in conv(A). This proves (2), including arbitrary weights and all
boundary atoms.

For atomic single-cell limits, write mu_z=w_z delta_bz. Apply (1) to
singletons at two same-parity bases. Their integer midpoint m is present,
and the positive mass inequality forces

    b_m=(b_z+b_w)/2.

Thus G={(z,b_z):z in P}, labeled by base parity, satisfies the lemma.
The resulting ACTUAL atomic measure has depth at least W/k, regardless
of hollow projections, nonaffine embedding, or unequal atom weights.
The cost-nine original-base allocation obstruction in the companion
hollow note therefore has no bearing on atomic centerpoint existence.

## 2. Dimension/tangent strata have disjoint exact parity budgets

The homothetic-domination argument in the slice source gives, for each
positive-weight source in an integer-output representation,

    mu_z >= theta_i^N (x -> theta_i x+c)_# mu_zi.          (3)

Each mu_z has a convex support S_z and is absolutely continuous in its
affine hull (or is an atom). Consequently (3) forces

    q_zi=q_z,    V_zi=V_z,                               (4)

where V_z is the tangent space of aff(S_z). If a source had smaller
dimension, its nonzero pushed measure would be concentrated on a set
of zero output measure. Support inclusion excludes larger dimension.
Equality of dimensions then makes the tangent spaces equal.

Partition P by the pairs (q,V). Let P_c be a stratum, W_c its total
mass, and k_c its number of occupied original parities. Each P_c is
lattice-complete in conv(P_c): every integer-output convex combination
of its bases has a positive output, and (4) puts that output in P_c.
Moreover distinct strata have disjoint parity sets. Indeed two bases
of the same parity have an integer midpoint, and (4) makes both sources
have its same pair (q,V). Hence

    sum_c k_c=k(P)<=2^n.                                 (5)

The same reasoning applies to dependence components within a stratum.
This decomposition has no overlapped source fibers and no arbitrary
allocation of densities. It is forced by the actual measure inequality.

For every stratum let

    D_c=conv union_(z in P_c) ({z} x S_z).

At every integer base its fiber is exactly S_z, with no other integer
fibers. To see the nontrivial inclusion, represent a point of D_c as a
finite convex combination of support points. Its base is integer only
at a point of P_c. Applying (1) to arbitrarily small positive-mass
neighborhoods places the represented continuous point in S_z. The reverse
inclusion is immediate. Thus the stratum support is an actual convex
mixed fiber family, even when its real-base fibers have larger dimension.

## 3. A direct intrinsic-support Helly bound

Here is a geometric lemma that needs neither density power concavity nor
a globally affine support graph.

Let D be compact convex, with finite nonempty integer base set P. Suppose
its exact nonempty integer fibers S_z are convex of affine dimension at
most q, and P is same-parity midpoint closed, occupying k parities. Then
S=union_(z in P) ({z} x S_z) has relative Helly number at most

    h=(q+1)k.                                             (6)

Proof: let a finite family of ambient convex sets C_i have intersection
missing S. At each integer base z, ordinary Helly in aff(S_z), applied
together with S_z, selects a set J_z of at most q+1 indices such that
S_z intersect intersection_(i in J_z) C_i is empty. For every nonempty
index set J of size at most q+1 put

    E_J=proj_base(D intersect intersection_(i in J) C_i).

These sets are convex; closedness is unnecessary. At every z in P at
least one E_J misses z. Their total intersection therefore misses P.
The finite parity Helly proof from Section 1, in the base coordinates,
selects at most k such E_J. The union I of their original index sets
has at most (q+1)k members. If a point of S satisfied all C_i for i in I,
its base would belong to every selected E_J, a contradiction. This
proves (6). Degenerate and lower-dimensional real-base sections do not
enter the argument.

For ANY finite positive Borel measure nu supported on this compact S,
relative Helly gives a point y in S satisfying

    nu(H)>=nu(S)/[(q+1)k]                                 (7)

for every closed halfspace H containing y. Here is a boundary-safe
compactness proof. Consider all closed convex sets K of mass greater
than (1-1/h)nu(S). Any at most h have positive intersection measure by
the union bound; (6) gives the finite intersection property on S.
Compactness of S selects a common point y. If a closed H through y had
mass less than nu(S)/h, its open complement would have mass greater
than (1-1/h)nu(S). Some slightly inset parallel CLOSED halfspace in
that complement still has mass greater than that threshold, by
continuity from below. It is one of the selected K and excludes y,
a contradiction. Entirely singular or atomic nu are allowed.

This is the usual mixed Helly centerpoint argument, applied to the
actual intrinsic support dimensions rather than the ambient continuous
dimension. It is not a new general sharp OC theorem.

## 4. Unconditional sharp-enough centers when every q_z<=1

Apply (7) separately to the exact strata of Section 2. The source measure
outside any chosen stratum only increases every halfspace mass. Therefore

    max_(y in original support) depth_mu(y)
       >= max_c W_c/[(q_c+1)k_c]
       >= W / sum_c ((q_c+1)k_c).                         (8)

The last inequality follows by choosing a largest mass-to-cost ratio.
It selects one deterministic actual support point; centers from different
strata are never averaged.

If every q_c is zero or one, let k_0 and k_1 be the total occupied parity
counts of the respective strata. Then

    max depth_mu >= W/(k_0+2k_1) >= W/(2k(P)).             (9)

For N>=1, Gamma_N=(N/(N+1))^N<=1/2. Thus (9) is at least
Gamma_N W/k(P). The all-atomic case has the sharper W/k(P) bound of
Section 1. These conclusions handle arbitrary hollow projections,
nonaffine physical offsets, overlapping maximal occupied faces, and
all closed ambient halfspaces.

In the positive-rate application with q_z<N, this completely settles the
EXISTENTIAL single-global-cell centerpoint for N=1 and N=2, equivalently
original continuous dimensions d=2 and d=3 when N=d-1. It does not move
an existing marked source anchor, prove capture by an existing selected
cap group, or split a group law among multiple cells. Those constraints
remain separate from existential centerpoint selection.

For q>=2 the direct bound 1/(q+1) falls below Gamma_N in the relevant
cases. Section 3 alone therefore does not solve the higher-rank problem.

## 5. Canonical integer graph lifts remove the hollow gluing obstruction

There is nevertheless a genuine ONE-BODY lift for each entire stratum,
with its full mass and exact occupied-parity count, if the integer base
is allowed its canonical graph lift. This uses the proved construction
in `candidate 2086e4eaa4bce465` and is a new
application of that existing construction, not a new canonical-lift lemma.

Fix a stratum P_c, its tangent V of dimension q<N, and set r=N-q.
Let b_z be the V-perpendicular coordinate of the affine support plane.
Support compatibility at every integer-output representation gives

    b_z=sum_i theta_i b_zi.                               (10)

Thus every coordinate of b belongs to the anchored representation space
L(P_c), even though b need not be affine in the original coordinates.
Choose an integer-valued rational basis for this representation space,
retaining the original base coordinates, and let Psi(P_c) be its canonical
integer graph lift. After identifying its saturated affine lattice with
Z^R, the archived canonical-lift theorem supplies:

* Psi(P_c) is lattice-complete;
* all anchored representations are preserved in both directions;
* exactly k_c parities are occupied, even if R exceeds n;
* b_z=B(Psi(z)) for one affine vector-valued function B.

For q>0 write mu_z=g_z H_q on b_z+V and f_z=g_z^(1/r).
Use the bounded upper-semicontinuous concave extension fbar_z on S_z.
For q=0 take fbar_z=W_z^(1/N). The unequal-radius-ball argument in the
slice source, applied only at integer outputs, gives

    fbar_z(sum_i theta_i x_i)>=sum_i theta_i fbar_zi(x_i). (11)

No real-base affine formula for b was needed to obtain this: at each
such representation (10) already aligns the parallel intrinsic planes.
Identify V isometrically with R^q and form

    K_z={(v,u) in R^q x R^r:
        b_z+v in S_z,
        |u|<=fbar_z(b_z+v)/omega_r^(1/r)}.                 (12)

Every K_z is a full-dimensional N-dimensional compact convex body, and
its ordinary volume projects exactly to mu_z. Equations (10)-(11) give
sum_i theta_i K_zi subset K_z at each integer-output representation.
Because Psi preserves precisely those representations, the convex body

    K_c=conv union_(z in P_c) ({Psi(z)} x K_z)             (13)

has exactly K_z as its integer fibers and no other integer fibers.
It has continuous dimension N and ONE affine physical projection

    (t,v,u) -> (pi(t), B(t)+v),                           (14)

where pi(Psi(z))=z. Its mixed ordinary volume pushes forward to the
ENTIRE stratum measure. All physical closed halfspaces pull back to closed
affine halfspaces (or the entire space when the functional is constant).
The projection of a mixed point belongs to an actual source support.
Thus all halfspace depths transfer in the useful direction.

There is no overlapped face cover and no density allocation in (13).
The companion cost-nine obstruction deliberately forbids this enlarged
integer base. Here that restriction is removed while exact parity is kept.

## 6. Precise inductive consequence and its limitation

Assume that the sharp theorem ALREADY PROVED in continuous dimension N
has the following occupied-parity form, for every integer rank R:

    every ordinary mixed convex body whose positive bases occupy k
    parities has a point of depth at least Gamma_N times mass/k.     (15)

Apply it to each K_c. Transfer its point by (14), then choose a stratum
with W_c/k_c>=W/k(P), using (5). This gives an actual original support
point of depth at least Gamma_N W/k(P) for the whole single-cell measure.
All hollow cases are covered by this conditional transfer.

If induction provides only Gamma_N/2^R, substituting it in (13) can lose
the original 2^n budget because R can increase. Equation (15) therefore
must be proved or explicitly retained in the inductive theorem. It is
not silently inferred from the ordinary statement with 2^R, and no
claim that (15) follows merely from Helly number is made here.

The unconditional advances are the arbitrary-embedding atomic application,
the disjoint dimension/tangent parity budgets, and the rank-at-most-one
existential center theorem. For higher rank, the canonical lift is an
exact geometric reduction with a clearly identified numerical input.
